# inertia-localize

> Laravel-first localization toolkit for Inertia apps. Laravel stays the source of truth for locales and translations; React and Vue adapters consume them through a small useTranslation() hook.

## Introduction

Source: https://inertia-localize.jiordiviera.me/docs/introduction

Inertia Localize brings Laravel's localization to Inertia applications through small React and
Vue adapters. Laravel remains the source of truth for supported locales and translation files;
the active locale and selected messages arrive as Inertia page props.

## Scope

Locale URL prefixes are not added by default. Laravel owns validation messages; this package
shares configured UI translation groups with the client. Frontend adapters use a small
translation helper, not a separate heavy i18n runtime.

## Packages

| Package | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `jiordiviera/inertia-localize` | Laravel service provider, middleware, Inertia shared prop |
| `@inertia-localize/core` | Framework-independent lookup + interpolation, shared types |
| `@inertia-localize/react` | `useTranslation()` hook for React |
| `@inertia-localize/vue` | `useTranslation()` composable for Vue |

Continue to [Installation](/docs/installation) to add the packages to an existing Laravel +
Inertia application.

---

## Installation

Source: https://inertia-localize.jiordiviera.me/docs/installation

Install the Laravel package and the adapter for your frontend. Packages are published
independently, so only install the adapter you use.

```sh
composer require jiordiviera/inertia-localize
npm install @inertia-localize/react  # or @inertia-localize/vue
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=inertia-localize-config
```

The service provider is registered through Laravel package discovery. Publishing writes
`config/inertia-localize.php`, which defines `default`, `fallback`, supported `locales`,
`session_key`, translation `groups`, and an optional `user_column`.

Next: [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart) wires up the locale route and reads a translation on the
frontend.

---

## Quickstart

Source: https://inertia-localize.jiordiviera.me/docs/quickstart

## 1. Configure locales and groups

```php
'locales' => ['en' => ['name' => 'English'], 'fr' => ['name' => 'Français']],
'groups' => ['ui'],
```

## 2. Add translations

Older Laravel apps may use `resources/lang` instead of `lang/`.

```php
// lang/en/ui.php
return ['greeting' => 'Hello :name'];
```

## 3. Register the locale route

Keep the switch route inside Laravel's session-enabled `web` middleware group.

```php
use InertiaLocalize\Http\Controllers\LocaleController;
use InertiaLocalize\Http\Middleware\SetLocale;

Route::post('/locale', LocaleController::class)->name('locale.switch');
Route::middleware(SetLocale::class)->group(function () {
    Route::get('/', HomeController::class);
});
```

## 4. Read a translation on the frontend

```tsx
import { useTranslation } from '@inertia-localize/react'

const { t, locale } = useTranslation()
t('ui.greeting', { name: 'Ada' }) // Hello Ada
```

Laravel automatically shares the `i18n` prop with Inertia, including `locale`, `fallback`,
`locales`, and flattened `messages` such as `ui.greeting`. See [The i18n shared
prop](/docs/i18n-prop) for the full shape.

---

## Configuration

Source: https://inertia-localize.jiordiviera.me/docs/configuration

`php artisan vendor:publish --tag=inertia-localize-config` writes `config/inertia-localize.php`:

```php
return [
    'default' => env('APP_LOCALE', 'en'),
    'fallback' => env('APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE', 'en'),
    'locales' => [
        'en' => ['name' => 'English'],
        'fr' => ['name' => 'Français'],
    ],
    'session_key' => 'locale',
    'groups' => ['ui'],
    'user_column' => null,
];
```

| Key | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `default` / `fallback` | Locale used when the session has no value, and when a message is missing |
| `locales` | Supported locale codes and display names, shared to the frontend as-is |
| `session_key` | Session key the active locale is stored under |
| `groups` | Laravel translation groups exported to the frontend, flattened to dot keys |
| `user_column` | Optional column on the authenticated user model used to persist locale across sessions |

The package does not depend on a frontend framework — this configuration is read entirely on
the Laravel side.

---

## Locale switching & sessions

Source: https://inertia-localize.jiordiviera.me/docs/locale-switching

The locale is session-based, not URL-based. POST the selected locale to the switch route, then
subsequent requests use that locale until it changes again.

```php
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Route;
use InertiaLocalize\Http\Controllers\LocaleController;
use InertiaLocalize\Http\Middleware\SetLocale;

Route::post('/locale', LocaleController::class)->name('locale.switch');

Route::middleware(SetLocale::class)->group(function () {
    Route::get('/', HomeController::class);
});
```

> Register `locale.switch` inside routes that already run in Laravel's session-enabled `web`
> middleware group — routes in `routes/web.php` start the session before route middleware runs.

Post `{ locale: 'fr' }` to `locale.switch`. Supported values are stored under the configured
`session_key`; unsupported values receive HTTP 422. On each request, `SetLocale` sets Laravel's
application locale from the session and falls back to the configured `default` when the session
value is missing or unsupported.

This session-first approach does not add locale URL prefixes or, by itself, persist a user
preference across devices — see below.

## Persisting on the user model

Set `user_column` in the config to remember an authenticated user's locale beyond the current
session, instead of only the session value.

---

## Translation groups

Source: https://inertia-localize.jiordiviera.me/docs/translation-groups

The package exports selected Laravel translation groups to the frontend — it does not ship a
separate translation format. List the groups to expose in `config/inertia-localize.php`:

```php
'groups' => ['ui'],
```

Each group corresponds to a Laravel language file per locale:

```php
// lang/en/ui.php
return [
    'greeting' => 'Hello :name',
    'actions' => [
        'save' => 'Save',
    ],
];
```

For the active locale, every configured group is loaded and flattened to dot keys prefixed by
the group name — `ui.greeting` and `ui.actions.save` in the example above. Flattening happens on
the Laravel side, so the frontend always receives a flat `messages` dictionary regardless of how
nested the underlying PHP array is.

If a translation key is missing, check the locale's language file, the configured `groups`, and
that the key includes its group prefix (`ui.greeting`, not `greeting`).

---

## The i18n shared prop

Source: https://inertia-localize.jiordiviera.me/docs/i18n-prop

The package automatically shares an `i18n` prop on every Inertia response — no controller
changes needed. It is available on the initial server-rendered page without a client fetch, and
is included in partial reloads.

```php
'i18n' => [
    'locale' => 'fr',
    'fallback' => 'en',
    'locales' => [
        ['code' => 'en', 'name' => 'English'],
        ['code' => 'fr', 'name' => 'Français'],
    ],
    'messages' => [
        'actions.save' => 'Enregistrer',
    ],
]
```

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `locale` | The active locale for this request |
| `fallback` | The configured fallback locale |
| `locales` | Every supported locale from config, as `{ code, name }` |
| `messages` | Flattened dot-key messages for the active locale's configured groups |

If `i18n` is missing from a page's props, confirm the route uses Inertia and Laravel's
session-enabled `web` middleware group — `SetLocale` and the prop sharing both depend on it.

---

## React adapter

Source: https://inertia-localize.jiordiviera.me/docs/react-adapter

`@inertia-localize/react` reads the current Inertia `i18n` prop directly — it does not keep a
second locale or message dictionary in React state.

```tsx
import { useTranslation } from '@inertia-localize/react'

export function Greeting() {
  const { t, locale, locales } = useTranslation()

  return (
    <p lang={locale}>
      {t('greeting.user', { name: 'Ada' })} ({locales.length} languages)
    </p>
  )
}
```

`useTranslation()` returns:

| Field | Type |
| --- | --- |
| `t(key, replacements?)` | Looks up a dot-key message and interpolates `:placeholder`s |
| `tChoice(key, count, replacements?)` | Selects a plural form using Laravel's `trans_choice` syntax — see [Interpolation](/docs/interpolation) |
| `locale` | Active locale code |
| `fallback` | Configured fallback locale code |
| `locales` | Every supported locale, as `{ code, name }` |

The consuming app must install compatible versions of `react` and `@inertiajs/react`.

## Switching locale

```tsx
import { useLocaleSwitch } from '@inertia-localize/react'

const { setLocale, switching } = useLocaleSwitch()
```

Posts to the locale-switch route (`/locale` by default, override with `{ url }`) via Inertia's
`router.post()`; the redirect it triggers refreshes `i18n` like any other visit. Also takes
`preserveScroll`, `preserveState`, `onSuccess`, and `onError`.

---

## Vue adapter

Source: https://inertia-localize.jiordiviera.me/docs/vue-adapter

`@inertia-localize/vue` reads the current Inertia page props directly and requires no Vue
plugin — just call the composable inside `<script setup>`.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useTranslation } from '@inertia-localize/vue'

const { t, locale, locales } = useTranslation()
</script>

<template>
  <p :lang="locale">
    {{ t('greeting.user', { name: 'Ada' }) }}
    ({{ locales.length }} languages)
  </p>
</template>
```

`useTranslation()` returns `t(key, replacements?)`, `tChoice(key, count, replacements?)` (Laravel
`trans_choice` syntax — see [Interpolation](/docs/interpolation)), plus computed refs for
`locale`, `fallback`, and `locales` — the same shape as the [React adapter](/docs/react-adapter),
so messages and dot keys behave identically across both.

The consuming app must install compatible versions of `vue` and `@inertiajs/vue3`.

## Switching locale

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useLocaleSwitch } from '@inertia-localize/vue'

const { setLocale, switching } = useLocaleSwitch()
</script>
```

Same shape as the [React adapter](/docs/react-adapter): posts to `/locale` by default (override
with `{ url }`) via Inertia's `router.post()`, plus `preserveScroll`, `preserveState`,
`onSuccess`, and `onError`. `switching` is a computed ref here instead of a plain boolean.

---

## Interpolation

Source: https://inertia-localize.jiordiviera.me/docs/interpolation

`@inertia-localize/core` powers lookup and interpolation for both adapters.

```ts
import { translate } from '@inertia-localize/core'

translate({ 'greeting.user': 'Hello :name' }, 'greeting.user', { name: 'Ada' })
// "Hello Ada"
```

Messages use flat dot-key dictionaries — the same shape the Laravel package produces from
translation groups. Placeholders use Laravel's `:name` syntax, not ICU or `{{mustache}}` syntax.
Replacements accept strings, numbers, and booleans; unknown placeholders remain unchanged.

## Missing keys

A missing key returns the key itself by default. Pass an explicit fallback as the fourth
argument when a friendlier default is needed:

```ts
translate({}, 'greeting.user', { name: 'Ada' }, { fallback: 'Hello :name' })
// "Hello Ada"
```

## Pluralization

`translateChoice(messages, key, count, replacements?, options?)` selects a plural form using
Laravel's `trans_choice` pipe-separated syntax — not ICU MessageFormat — so lang files stay the
same whether an app also calls `trans_choice()` server-side:

```ts
import { translateChoice } from '@inertia-localize/core'

const messages = {
  'cart.items': '{0} No items|{1} One item|[2,*] :count items',
}

translateChoice(messages, 'cart.items', 0) // "No items"
translateChoice(messages, 'cart.items', 1) // "One item"
translateChoice(messages, 'cart.items', 5) // "5 items"
```

Each segment may start with an exact `{n}` or inclusive range `[n,m]` selector (`*` for
infinity); the first matching segment wins, falling back to the last one. Without any explicit
selector, only the plain 2-segment `singular|plural` shape resolves (`count === 1` picks the
first) — for 3+ forms, use explicit ranges rather than relying on locale-specific plural rules,
which this package doesn't implement. `:count` is always available for interpolation and
overrides a same-named entry in `replacements`, matching `trans_choice`.

---

## API reference

Source: https://inertia-localize.jiordiviera.me/docs/api-reference

## `@inertia-localize/core`

- `translate(messages, key, replacements?, { fallback }?)` — dot-key lookup with `:name`
  interpolation.
- Shared types: `LocaleCode`, `LocaleMetadata`, `MessageDictionary`, `TranslationReplacements`,
  `I18nProps`. `I18nProps` matches the Laravel/Inertia contract: active locale, fallback locale,
  available locales, and the current flat message dictionary.

## `@inertia-localize/react`

- `useTranslation()` &rarr; `{ t, locale, fallback, locales }`

## `@inertia-localize/vue`

- `useTranslation()` &rarr; `{ t, locale, fallback, locales }` (`locale`, `fallback`, `locales`
  are computed refs)

## Laravel package (`jiordiviera/inertia-localize`)

- `InertiaLocalize\Http\Middleware\SetLocale` &mdash; resolves the active locale from session,
  applies it to the request.
- `InertiaLocalize\Http\Controllers\LocaleController` &mdash; handles `POST` to the locale
  switch route.
- Shared Inertia prop: `i18n` &mdash; see [The i18n shared prop](/docs/i18n-prop).
- Config: `config/inertia-localize.php` &mdash; see [Configuration](/docs/configuration).

---

## Troubleshooting

Source: https://inertia-localize.jiordiviera.me/docs/troubleshooting

## `i18n` prop is missing

Confirm the route renders through Inertia and runs inside Laravel's session-enabled `web`
middleware group. The shared prop and `SetLocale` both depend on an active session.

## A translation key renders as-is

`translate()` returns the key itself when it isn't found. Check, in order:

1. The locale's language file has the key (`lang/en/ui.php`).
2. The key's group is listed in `config('inertia-localize.groups')`.
3. The key you're calling includes its group prefix &mdash; `ui.greeting`, not `greeting`.

## Switching locale doesn't persist

The switch route must be registered inside the `web` middleware group so the session is
available. If you need the locale to persist across sessions for a signed-in user, set
`user_column` in the config &mdash; see [Locale switching &
sessions](/docs/locale-switching#persisting-on-the-user-model).

## Locale switch POST returns 422

The posted `locale` value isn't in `config('inertia-localize.locales')`. Only configured locale
codes are accepted.

---

## Compatibility

Source: https://inertia-localize.jiordiviera.me/docs/compatibility

## Laravel package

| Requirement | Versions |
| --- | --- |
| PHP | &ge;8.2 |
| Laravel (`illuminate/*`) | ^11.0 &#124; ^12.0 &#124; ^13.0 |
| `inertiajs/inertia-laravel` | ^2.0 &#124; ^3.0 |

## `@inertia-localize/react`

| Requirement | Versions |
| --- | --- |
| `react` | ^16.9.0 &#124; ^17.0.0 &#124; ^18.0.0 &#124; ^19.0.0 |
| `@inertiajs/react` | ^2.0.0 &#124; ^3.0.0 |

## `@inertia-localize/vue`

| Requirement | Versions |
| --- | --- |
| `vue` | ^3.0.0 |
| `@inertiajs/vue3` | ^2.0.0 &#124; ^3.0.0 |

`@inertia-localize/core` has no peer dependencies &mdash; it's plain TypeScript shared by both
adapters.
